title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find).

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size stays on that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane) until you call this tool again with preset "desktop", so reset it once you are done testing. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent, 5 touch points, and mouse-to-touch translation (hover stops producing hover states). Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.4.1/skills/systematic-debugging

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

98	### 2.3 Basket merge: mode, default, and the same-product match rules
99	
100	`mergeBasket` request parameter `productItemMergeMode`:
101	`"higher_quantity" | "sum_quantities" | "saved_quantity" | "separate_item"`.
102	SDK doc: *"By default, the higher of the two basket quantities is used for each product."*
103	
104	Same-product match requires **all** of these to be equal:
105	> shipment · productId · option values · wishlist reference · inventory list id ·
106	> gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments
107	
108	> *"If any of the listed values don't match, then the item in the previous shopper's basket is
109	> copied to a **new line item** in the current shopper's basket."*
110	
111	Consequence: `higher_quantity` protects only the single-line case. Two lines of the same SKU that
112	differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag do **not** merge, and their quantities coexist —
113	so a SKU total can exceed the cap without any single line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic
114	differentiators are **Collect in Boutique** (separate shipment) and **boutique vs warehouse
115	inventory lists** (CAI-022). At plain cart with no fulfilment choice made, both baskets sit in the
116	same default shipment and inventory list, so they DO match and 2 + 2 → 2 under the default.
117	
118	### 2.4 Where merge is called, and with what
119	
120	Four base call sites, **all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`** (no merge mode):
121	- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js`
122	- `.../app/pages/login/index.jsx`
123	- `.../app/pages/social-login-redirect/index.jsx`
124	- `.../app/pages/checkout/partials/contact-info.jsx`
125	
126	`use-auth-modal.js` carries the comment *"if you change logic here, also change it in login page"* —
127	Salesforce knows the invariant is duplicated.
128	
129	**The invariant is login-only, deliberately not register:**
130	> *"we only want to merge basket when the user is logged in as a recurring user — only recurring
131	> users trigger the login mutation, new user triggers register mutation"*
132	
133	Reason holds: a brand-new customer has no prior basket, so their guest basket simply becomes theirs.

467	### SFCC-250 — Maximum Purchase Quantity · 9 ACs · 9 of 9 addressed
468	
469	The rule: **max 3 units per SKU (same size + colour) per order** — CAI-017, `cart.md` §2.
470	The card states outright it is *not* a component build story: the stepper is 271's, the inline
471	warning is 795's, the page-level banner is 404's.
472	
473	| Decision | Value |
474	|---|---|
475	| Max value | No BM setting exists (§2.1). Promote `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` out of `product-detail/index.tsx:123` into a shared constant; cart reads the same one. Re-typing `3` would breach `conventions.md`'s no-magic-numbers rule. |
476	| Threshold | **`>=`**, not the AC's literal "equals" — otherwise a line already holding 4 fails the check and the `+` stays live exactly when it matters. Matches the PDP. |
477	| Scope of the limit | **Per line item.** Rationale: the SKU is already size *and* colour, so in normal shopping one line **is** one SKU. |
478	| Merge mode | **`sum_quantities`.** AC5's "combined quantity ... exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. |
479	| Cap shape | **Consolidate to one line at 3.** Free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single *"merged line item"* for matching products. |
480	| Merge call | **Zimmermann-owned**, placed where `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — completing the half-implemented pairing in §2.5, and covering all four consumers at once. |
481	| Callback order | **merge → cap → 272's pending wishlist resume.** The wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing the order moves a quantity the shopper never saw. |
482	| Render guard | Secondary backstop for baskets that went over some other way (stale session, order-on-behalf). **No-ops while any basket mutation is in flight** via React Query's `useIsMutating()`, so it cannot race the callback. |
483	| Shared logic | Merge-and-cap lives in **its own small function**, called by both the callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies. |
484	| Flash (briefly showing 4) | **No action.** Observe the real behaviour first. |
485	| Loop guard | **Keep it** — distinct from the flash. Without it, a write-on-render can fire repeatedly (concurrent writes racing on one line item; or endless retries if the server refuses), which can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket. One correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error. |

764	   **require** action".
765	=> **This is a message aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions.** The
766	   "half a day" estimate given when deciding whether to pull 404 forward was wrong by a lot.

# Session notes — Cart bundle (SFCC-11), pre-build decisions

> **BUILD HANDOFF: start at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/HANDOFF.md`.**
> Planning is CLOSED. Gate is clean, no blockers. Single PR, 18 commits, branch
> `feature/SFCC-11_cart` off `develop` @ `71025f18`. This file is the decision record and the full
> Figma spec; `plan.md` is the executable plan; `findings.md` is the gate.


**Written:** 2026-09-16
**Branch at time of writing:** `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (NOT the build branch — a
fresh `feature/*` off `develop` is needed before any cart work starts)
**Scope:** card-by-card requirements pass over 7 Cart stories, ahead of a bundled build.
**Status:** all 7 cards read, all ACs pulled and adjudicated. No code written. No Jira updated.

The ACs do **not** live in the Jira description — they are in custom field `customfield_10231`
("Acceptance Criteria", project-scoped, textarea). Fetching only the description misses them
entirely. Some return plain text, some return ADF (`{type: "doc"}`) — SFCC-315/270/795 came back
as ADF and needed flattening.

---

## 1. The bundle

All 7 are Epic SFCC-11 (Cart), SFCC Sprint 5 (active, 2026-09-07 → 2026-09-21), label `Squad-A`,
assigned to Marcel, status **Ready for Development**.

| Card | Title | Priority | Reqs |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-315 | Drawer Component (Cart Variation) – PWA Kit Component | High | CAI-006 |
| SFCC-270 | Cart Item Component UI (Part 1) – PWA Kit Component | High | CAI-006 |
| SFCC-795 | Cart Item Component UI (Part 2) – PWA Kit Component | Medium | — |
| SFCC-271 | Cart Item Component – Quantity Stepper | High | CAI-007 |
| SFCC-272 | Cart Item – Remove and Wishlist Actions | High | CAI-008, CAI-018 |
| SFCC-250 | Cart – Maximum Purchase Quantity Enforcement per SKU | Medium | CAI-017, PRD-011 |
| SFCC-275 | Cart Page – Button Group | High | CAI-010 |

### Bundle-shape decision

One gather pass and one plan across all 7 (done — this document). **Not** one mega-PR.
Rationale: a single PR converts 7 independently-mergeable units into one all-or-nothing unit;
one change-requested story would block the other six. Cart also spans two squads' Tier 2
ownership (`order-summary`/`promo-code` = Squad A, `product-item` = Squad B), so a single PR pulls
in both code-owner reviews at once, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires explicit scope
confirmation before touching more than one protection tier in one change.

**Exception:** SFCC-250 and SFCC-272 are welded at the cart's `onAuthSuccess` seam (see §5) and
build as one PR. Accepted deliberately.

### A real CI consequence, not yet addressed

`qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job has no **`cart`** e2e area. The existing areas are `homepage`,
`checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`. `e2e-localhost` only runs when every
e2e-relevant changed file falls inside exactly one area's allow-list — otherwise it resolves to
`e2e_scope: skip` and **does not run at all** on that PR. So every cart PR currently gets no
PR-time E2E. Adding a `cart` allow-list group + `@cart` tags is a deliberate step in the plan, not
something to discover afterwards. See `.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E.

---

## 2. Verified findings (evidence-backed — re-verify before relying on any of these)

### 2.1 SFCC has no max-order-quantity field. The frontend constant IS the implementation.

- `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts` contains `minOrderQuantity` (6 occurrences) and
  `stepQuantity`. **No `maxOrderQuantity` anywhere.**
- Live probe against the dev sandbox (site `ZimmermannAU`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`, SLAS private-client
  `client_credentials` guest token, mirroring `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `liveCheckSfcc`), two real
  products: quantity-related keys returned are `inventory`, `minOrderQuantity`, `stepQuantity`.
  `maxOrderQuantity` absent.
- Custom attributes returned (so `c_*` exposure is working): `c_ap21Category`, `c_careInstructions`,
  `c_countryOfOrigin`, `c_environmentalNotes`, `c_fabricComposition`, `c_hsCode`, `c_isFinalSale`,
  `c_isNew`, `c_isSale`, `c_label`, `c_relatedMasterProductID`, `c_season`, `c_sizeFit`,
  `c_sizeGuide`, `c_styleId`, `c_styleNumber`, `c_stylingNotes`, `c_relatedSwatches`,
  `c_showEnvironmentalNote`. **None is a max-quantity attribute.**
- **Caveat:** dev sandbox only, 2 products. A custom attribute on sit/uat is not ruled out — but
  with no standard field at all, unlikely.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:123`:
  `/** Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform max-order-quantity field. */`
  `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3;` — passed to `ProductView` as `maxOrderQuantity` at line 1282.
- **Conflict to record:** SFCC-268 "PDP – Maximum Purchase Quantity – **BM Config**" is
  *Ready for SIT* (Done, Sprint 3, Victor Crisostomo). Nothing reachable from the Shopper API was
  configured. 250's ACs all say "the **configured** maximum of 3".

### 2.2 The existing PDP enforcement shape (reusable)

`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `isMaxOrderQtyReached`:
```
if (maxOrderQuantity == null) return false;          // null = unrestricted
const inBag = basketProductItems
  .filter((item) => item.productId === productId)     // per SKU
  .reduce((sum, item) => sum + (item.quantity ?? 0), 0);  // summed ACROSS line items
return inBag >= maxOrderQuantity;                     // >=, not ==
```
Gates `handleAddToBag` (hard block) and caps `QuantityPicker`'s `max`. Tests/stories at 2, 3, null.
Note it **sums across line items** — i.e. the existing code already assumes one SKU can occupy more
than one line.

### 2.3 Basket merge: mode, default, and the same-product match rules

`mergeBasket` request parameter `productItemMergeMode`:
`"higher_quantity" | "sum_quantities" | "saved_quantity" | "separate_item"`.
SDK doc: *"By default, the higher of the two basket quantities is used for each product."*

Same-product match requires **all** of these to be equal:
> shipment · productId · option values · wishlist reference · inventory list id ·
> gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments

> *"If any of the listed values don't match, then the item in the previous shopper's basket is
> copied to a **new line item** in the current shopper's basket."*

Consequence: `higher_quantity` protects only the single-line case. Two lines of the same SKU that
differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag do **not** merge, and their quantities coexist —
so a SKU total can exceed the cap without any single line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic
differentiators are **Collect in Boutique** (separate shipment) and **boutique vs warehouse
inventory lists** (CAI-022). At plain cart with no fulfilment choice made, both baskets sit in the
same default shipment and inventory list, so they DO match and 2 + 2 → 2 under the default.

### 2.4 Where merge is called, and with what

Four base call sites, **all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`** (no merge mode):
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js`
- `.../app/pages/login/index.jsx`
- `.../app/pages/social-login-redirect/index.jsx`
- `.../app/pages/checkout/partials/contact-info.jsx`

`use-auth-modal.js` carries the comment *"if you change logic here, also change it in login page"* —
Salesforce knows the invariant is duplicated.

**The invariant is login-only, deliberately not register:**
> *"we only want to merge basket when the user is logged in as a recurring user — only recurring
> users trigger the login mutation, new user triggers register mutation"*

Reason holds: a brand-new customer has no prior basket, so their guest basket simply becomes theirs.

### 2.5 No Zimmermann code merges baskets, and one route is a defect

- `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` → **empty.**
- `commerce-sdk-react` contains `mergeBasket` only as a mutation definition
  (`hooks/ShopperBaskets/mutation.js`), never in `auth/` — **the SDK does not auto-merge on login.**

`useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s three auth routes:

| Route | Merges? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Social IDP (`AuthorizeIDP`) | Yes — redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges | ✅ fine |
| Create account (`useAuthModal(REGISTER_VIEW)`) | No — base deliberately skips register | ✅ correct by design |
| **Passwordless OTP (`LoginPasswordlessUser`)** | **No** | ❌ **DEFECT** |

Passwordless OTP is a recurring-user login, which is exactly the case the invariant exists for.
Base `use-auth-modal` has its own passwordless flow **and pairs it with the merge**;
`useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge
across. Without a merge, SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket
is orphaned — **the shopper's items are lost, not mis-counted.**

Affects all four consumers of the hook: the cart (new), `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`,
`product-view`.

**This is code-inferred, not yet observed live. Verify before filing** — guest adds an item, opens
the cart, signs in with the email code, check whether the item survives.

### 2.6 `PendingWishlistIntent` carries no product

`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`:
`type PendingWishlistIntent = { intentId: string; timestamp: number }`, session-stored under
`zimmPendingWishlistAction`, 5-minute max age, scoped by `intentId` so only the initiating instance
replays. Fine for the three existing callers (a PDP has one product; the header's action isn't
product-specific). **The cart is the first caller with N products**, so on the social-redirect route
the resumed `onAuthSuccess` has no idea which line item the shopper clicked.

### 2.7 No cart overrides exist at all

Absent: `overrides/app/pages/cart`, `overrides/app/components/cart`,
`overrides/app/components/order-summary`, `overrides/app/components/product-item`.
`overrides/app/pages/checkout` exists but contains only `partials/payment.tsx` + its story —
`contact-info` is **not** overridden.
No `overrides/app/pages/login` — base login page still in use.

### 2.8 Order summary updates for free

Base `pages/cart/index.jsx` calls `useCurrentBasket()`, mutates via
`updateItemInBasketMutation.mutateAsync`, and passes the same basket object to `<OrderSummary>`.
So "order summary updates when quantity changes" is a consequence of basket cache invalidation, not
code any stepper story owns. Base `components/order-summary/index.jsx` exists and has no override —
so SFCC-274 is "restyle it to Figma", not "build one that doesn't exist".

### 2.9 Base `product-item` is a shared SFCC internal

Imported by `components/product-item-list`, `pages/account/wishlist`, `pages/cart`.
`protectedFiles.md` puts `overrides/app/components/product-item/` at **Tier 2, Squad B-owned
(notify Squad A)**.

### 2.10 Base wishlist handler silently no-ops for guests

`pages/cart/index.jsx`, `handleAddToWishlist`:
```
if (!customerId || !wishlist) { return }
```
A guest clicking Move to Wishlist gets **nothing**. `cart.md` §2 (CAI-008) requires the opposite:
*"an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first."*
The same handler already implements the `isItemInWishlist` branch and surfaces success via a Chakra
toast (`TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST`) with a "View Wishlist" action button.

### 2.11 ZimmButton variants and the 24px target size

Variants: `primary`, `primaryInverse`, `secondary`, `secondaryInverse`, `social`, `icon`,
`iconInverse`. Sizes: `lg`, `sm`, `social`, `icon`.
`sizes.icon` = `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)`; `spacing.ts` resolves `xl` to `1.5rem` = **24px**,
chosen deliberately — the inline comment reads *"WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target size.
SFCC-55's accessibility note names this control specifically."* It also explains why it is
`minW`/`minH` and not padding: Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0` as a style prop, so
padding declared in the recipe is silently discarded (a previous `p: 'xs'` rendered 16×16).

`actionSizes.height` = `lg: 52px`, `md: 40px` (Figma-confirmed).
**`overrideStyling.md` is stale here:** it still cites `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`
as standing provisional exceptions. Those constants no longer exist in `zimmButton.css.ts`; the only
remaining provisional is `BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG = '80px' // audit-allow: provisional`.

### 2.12 Domestic vs international is already modelled

`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `CountryConfig`:
`urlSlug`, `sfccSiteId`, `locale`, `currency`, `shippingCountry`, `checkoutOwner`, `globalEPricing`,
`boutiqueRegion`. `checkoutOwner`'s own doc comment:
> *"Checkout owner for this site's domestic path. Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field
> at PDP/cart level — not only at the checkout page."*

Read via `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` (matches on `sfccSiteId` + locale to disambiguate
the en-GB collision between the UK site and EU English; falls back to AU on an unrecognised site).

### 2.13 Base Checkout CTA has no region branch

`pages/cart/partials/cart-cta.jsx` → `<Button as={Link} to="/checkout">` unconditionally.
So international shoppers already land on SFCC checkout today; leaving that path alone is the
current behaviour, not a regression. The same file also uses `useExpressCheckoutEnabled()`, which
already gates express buttons on the cart — worth checking before writing new show/hide logic.

### 2.14 Empty-state precedent

`overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (on `origin/feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`,
PR #116 — **not merged to develop**). Pattern, per its own JSDoc: structure ported from base
`EmptyCart` (`pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`) as `Box > Center > Stack`; `isRegistered`-branched
body copy; `Button as={Link}` using the **base SFCC `Link`** (not raw react-router) so the CTA href
gets multi-site prefixing via `use-multi-site`'s `buildUrl`; `useIntl` called directly in the leaf
under the Context-backed exception in `components.md`; private single-parent sub-component so no
story/test of its own; decision log at the bottom of the file.

That file made **autonomous styling judgement calls** because it had no design at all. The cart
does have one (SFCC-315 carries an Empty Cart screenshot), so take **structure** from the precedent
and **visuals from Figma** — do not repeat the token-invention.

### 2.15 House pattern for a design-vs-standard deviation

From `zimmButton.css.ts`: cite the specific criterion, name where the requirement came from, explain
any mechanical gotcha, and name what is deferred and who owns it. Examples in that file: the 2.5.8
note above, and the focus-ring block — *"Replaces the previous outline:none + bg-swap, which gave the
primary variant an invisible focus state (#191919 default vs #000000 focus) — a WCAG 2.4.7 failure...
Dark-surface / inverse ring (grey-white) is the separate deferred inverse-focus item, owned with the
UI designer."*

**Annotate inline, log with the designer, ship. Do not escalate or block.**

---

## 3. A reading correction worth keeping

I over-read cross-references three times in this session. A `see SFCC-NNN` / "Relates to" in an AC
usually points at **where the design or detail lives**, not at a gate. Treat it as a dependency only
when the card says so outright — as SFCC-272's description does (*"This story is dependent on other
components being developed, including..."*) and SFCC-250's does (*"The following components must be
developed before this story can be implemented end to end"*).

Wrongly called blocked and later corrected: SFCC-271 (on 274), SFCC-275 (on 816), and AC2 of
SFCC-272 (on 277).

---

## 4. Per-card decisions

### SFCC-315 — Drawer (Cart Variation) · 9 ACs · all buildable

ACs: header `"BAG • [count]"` with right-aligned X / `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` when empty; count updates
dynamically without reload; slides in from the right, right portion on desktop+tablet with a
non-interactive overlaid background, **full screen on mobile**; closes via X, outside click, and
Escape with **focus returned to the trigger**; no loss of page state or scroll position on close;
responsive per Figma.

- Build as a **new organism wrapping `ZimmDrawer`**, not as a modification to the atom and not as an
  override of base `pages/cart`.
- Reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already has `finalFocusRef` (AC7), the overlay, right placement, size variants,
  mobile full-height, and concurrent-instance scroll-lock coordination — all from SFCC-831/926.
- AC3's dynamic count comes free from basket cache invalidation.
- AC8: verify the scroll-lock **restores** position on close rather than merely unlocking.
- **315 owns the empty-state *header text* only.** The empty *body* is SFCC-277's. Clean split.
- 315 is a dependency for SFCC-270, 274, 316, 318, 404 — and **SFCC-316 (Zimmermann Benefits –
  Contentful) is Sprint 5, Ready for Development, assigned to Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz.** Someone else's
  active-sprint card is waiting on this. **Ship 315 first and standalone.**

### SFCC-270 — Cart Item UI Part 1 · 9 ACs · all buildable

ACs: per line item — image; name to the right of the image; price; selected colour; selected size;
quantity with `+`/`–` either side; multiple items each individually identifiable; Remove and Wishlist
as **underlined text links below the stepper**; on mobile nothing truncated or hidden.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): override base `product-item`.** Cart keeps using it. Separately,
upcoming wishlist work moves the account wishlist page onto `ZimmProductCard` (which already has a
`variation: 'wishlist'` with `showRemove`), so it stops consuming `product-item` at that point.

Accurate consumer map — **two chains only**:
```
pages/cart  ->  components/product-item-list  ->  components/product-item
pages/account/wishlist  ->  components/product-item          (direct)
```
Checkout does **not** use it. The base has two separate line-item systems: `product-item` (the full
interactive row) and `item-variant/*` (a read-only composition used by `order-summary`, i.e. the
checkout summaries).

**Copy-first scope — 3 files** from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/`:
`index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB),
each to `.tsx`. Base's own `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` are not copied — write our own.

**The finding that changes the size of the job:** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content
through **five more base components** — `components/item-variant` plus `item-variant/item-image`,
`item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price`. So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's
*structure and controls*; the *content pieces* still come from `item-variant/*`. Styling those to
Figma means either overriding `item-variant/*` too — which also changes `order-summary`, and
therefore the checkout summaries — or not using them inside our override and composing the content
ourselves. **Decide this before starting: it is the difference between a 3-file override and an
8-file one with checkout blast radius.**

**`shared/ui` barrel trap applies.** `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`.
Per the known trap, overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — 208 base files
import the barrel, so only overriding the barrel itself has any effect.

**Bridge-pattern requirement:** because `product-item` is used internally by base components, the
override's **default export must stay API-compatible** (full original prop surface) so
`product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working. Per `overrideStyling.md`, put brand styling
in a **theme recipe**, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second
export that `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): Option B — override `item-variant/*` as well. 8 files.**
`product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}` +
`item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}`, all to `.tsx`.

Verified before deciding: **every consumer of `item-variant/*` is base/OOTB with no Zimmermann
design or development**, so brand styling landing on them is an upgrade toward Zimmermann, not a
regression from it. Full consumer list — `components/order-summary` (no override),
`components/multiship/multiship-order-summary`, `pages/account/order-detail` (account has zero
overrides), `pages/account/wishlist/partials/wishlist-primary-action` +
`wishlist-secondary-button-group` (and wishlist is migrating to `ZimmProductCard` anyway),
`pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group` (base cart page, replaced by the drawer),
`pages/checkout/partials/{pickup-address,product-shipping-address-card,shipping-product-cards}`
(checkout override is only `payment.tsx`), `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-product-shipping-address-card`.

**`pages/confirmation` is NOT in the blast radius** — `overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx`
already exists and does not use `item-variant`, so the base confirmation page is shadowed and never
renders. That was the one surface worth worrying about (a shopper sees it after paying).

**Two requirements for the override, both load-bearing:**
1. **Keep the defaults-then-spread order.** Callers set their own geometry —
   `order-summary` does `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` — and must keep winning.
   Write `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse, or you break layouts that work
   today. `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` already have it right.
2. **Fix `item-name` while in there.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread
   *before* the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after; no base caller
   passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.

**Deferred consequence, accepted:** when checkout is designed it will inherit cart-derived
line-item styling it never specified. Whoever picks up checkout should know why it already looks
part-branded.

**Governance:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/` is **Tier 2, Squad B-owned (notify Squad A)**
per `protectedFiles.md`. CODEOWNERS will request Squad B's review on a Squad A ticket.

**Interim consequence, low risk:** while the account wishlist page still consumes `product-item`, our
override's styling reaches it too. `overrides/app/pages/` contains no account pages at all — account
is entirely base and unstyled today — so the exposure is minimal until the wishlist migration lands.

### SFCC-271 — Quantity Stepper · 4 ACs · all buildable

ACs: `+` increments by 1 with item total and order summary updating; `–` decrements when quantity > 1;
at quantity 1 the `–` is disabled and quantity stays 1; drawer count (`Bag 3`) and order summary both
update without a full page load.

- **No SFCC-274 dependency** — see §2.8. Deliverable is the mutation call, the debounce, the
  optimistic local quantity, and the error rollback. The summary updating falls out of invalidation.
- Courtesy heads-up to Hazel (SFCC-274's assignee): the stepper lands first and sets the
  invalidation contract; the order summary should read basket state via `useCurrentBasket()` rather
  than holding its own copy.

### SFCC-795 — Cart Item UI Part 2 · the largest card

Groups: default state (restates 270); stepper states (quantity 1 → `–` disabled/greyed; > 1 → both
enabled; at max → `+` disabled/greyed; fully OOS or unavailable → **both** disabled/greyed); error
state (red inline message beneath the stepper — OOS, Partially OOS, Unavailable, copy supplied);
promotional price ("Was $X" / "Now $Y" replacing standard price, plus a discount label beneath the

### SFCC-250 — Maximum Purchase Quantity · 9 ACs · 9 of 9 addressed

The rule: **max 3 units per SKU (same size + colour) per order** — CAI-017, `cart.md` §2.
The card states outright it is *not* a component build story: the stepper is 271's, the inline
warning is 795's, the page-level banner is 404's.

| Decision | Value |
|---|---|
| Max value | No BM setting exists (§2.1). Promote `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` out of `product-detail/index.tsx:123` into a shared constant; cart reads the same one. Re-typing `3` would breach `conventions.md`'s no-magic-numbers rule. |
| Threshold | **`>=`**, not the AC's literal "equals" — otherwise a line already holding 4 fails the check and the `+` stays live exactly when it matters. Matches the PDP. |
| Scope of the limit | **Per line item.** Rationale: the SKU is already size *and* colour, so in normal shopping one line **is** one SKU. |
| Merge mode | **`sum_quantities`.** AC5's "combined quantity ... exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. |
| Cap shape | **Consolidate to one line at 3.** Free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single *"merged line item"* for matching products. |
| Merge call | **Zimmermann-owned**, placed where `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — completing the half-implemented pairing in §2.5, and covering all four consumers at once. |
| Callback order | **merge → cap → 272's pending wishlist resume.** The wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing the order moves a quantity the shopper never saw. |
| Render guard | Secondary backstop for baskets that went over some other way (stale session, order-on-behalf). **No-ops while any basket mutation is in flight** via React Query's `useIsMutating()`, so it cannot race the callback. |
| Shared logic | Merge-and-cap lives in **its own small function**, called by both the callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies. |
| Flash (briefly showing 4) | **No action.** Observe the real behaviour first. |
| Loop guard | **Keep it** — distinct from the flash. Without it, a write-on-render can fire repeatedly (concurrent writes racing on one line item; or endless retries if the server refuses), which can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket. One correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error. |

AC disposition: **1, 2** build (needs 271, 795) · **3, 8** → SFCC-404 · **4, 9** nothing to build
(negative assertions; Apple/Google Pay buttons don't exist yet anyway) · **5** build ·
**6, 7** free — they are AC1 and AC2's rules applied to a post-merge state, and a consolidated line
at 3 satisfies per-line `>=`.

**Accepted consequence of `sum_quantities`, recorded deliberately:** it changes **every** merge, not
just over-max ones. A guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it —
today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. **It must go in a
comment on the card**, because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to
know two items is intended rather than a bug.

**Deliberate boundary, recorded so it isn't mistaken for an oversight:** per-line enforcement means
a SKU split across two lines can total more than 3 without either line hitting max. That case only
arises from the merge splitting a line, which is what AC5 exists to catch. In that same edge case the
PDP (which sums per SKU) and the cart (per line) apply different rules.

1	import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
2	import type { ShopperBasketsV2Types } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
3	import { useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
5	
6	/**
7	 * The minimal basket shape this hook needs, regardless of which caller supplies it: the
8	 * post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, wired in this step) passes the resolved value
9	 * of its own `mergeBasket` mutation directly; the cart drawer's render guard
10	 * (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, step 4.6 — not yet built) will pass its
11	 * own `useCurrentBasket()` data. `Pick`-narrowed, matching `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own established
12	 * pattern for taking an untyped-at-the-edges SDK response and narrowing it to only the fields a
13	 * pure function actually reads, rather than depending on the exact generic SDK response type
14	 * either caller's own mutation/query hook happens to produce.
15	 */
16	export type CartCapBasket = Pick<ShopperBasketsV2Types.Basket, 'basketId' | 'lastModified' | 'productItems'>;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Outcome of one `capBasketQuantities` call. A discriminated union (typescript.md's guidance for
20	 * variant/state modelling) rather than a boolean-plus-optional-error: each branch is something a
21	 * caller could reasonably want to react to differently, and no AC or copy exists yet for any of
22	 * them (that is `useCartMessages`, step 4.3, not built) — this file only reports what happened,
23	 * it does not decide what the shopper sees.
24	 */
25	// Bounded so a caller can never be blocked indefinitely by an unrelated stuck mutation — on
26	// timeout it proceeds anyway rather than dropping the shopper's action. Generous against a real
27	// merge-then-cap round trip (two sequential SCAPI writes), which measured ~400ms end to end.
28	const CART_WRITE_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 4000;
29	const CART_WRITE_SETTLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 80;
30	
31	export type CartCapResult =
32	  | { status: 'not-needed' }
33	  | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'mutation-in-flight' | 'already-attempted-this-version' }
34	  | { status: 'corrected' }
35	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
36	
37	/**
38	 * `getMaxOrderQuantity` is typed for a SCAPI product response (`id: string` required — see
39	 * `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`). A basket line item has no `id` field at all: only
40	 * `itemId`/`productId` (confirmed against the generated `BasketProductItem` type — verified via
41	 * a throwaway `tsc` repro that assigning a same-shaped object to a type requiring `id` fails
42	 * with "Property 'id' is missing"), so passing one directly does not type-check, despite it
43	 * carrying the same `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all a real `c_maxOrderQuantity` value would
44	 * arrive through once SFCC-268 ships. `product-item/index.tsx` already lives with the identical
45	 * gap at its own `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` call site (`type SfccProduct = any`, lines 171
46	 * and 331) — narrowed here with an explicit, commented cast instead of a bare `any` parameter,
47	 * per typescript.md's "no `any` without an inline comment" rule.
48	 */
49	const getLineMaxOrderQuantity = (item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem): number =>
50	  getMaxOrderQuantity(item as unknown as Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]);
51	
52	/**
53	 * A line needs correction once its quantity exceeds the cap — i.e. once it reaches the smallest
54	 * over-cap value (`max + 1`; `4` when `max` is `3`) or anything above it. Written as `quantity >
55	 * max` rather than comparing against a separately-named `max + 1` boundary, but the two are the
56	 * same comparison: this must be a "the whole range above the boundary" check, not an
57	 * exact-equality check against a single value — an equality check against `max + 1` alone would
58	 * correctly catch a line at 4 but wrongly leave a line at 5 or more uncorrected, which is
59	 * observably wrong against this hook's own test fixture (a line at 5 must reduce to 3, not stay
60	 * at 5).
61	 */
62	const needsQuantityCorrection = (
63	  item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem,
64	): item is ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem & { quantity: number } =>
65	  typeof item.quantity === 'number' && item.quantity > getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item);
66	
67	/**
68	 * SFCC baskets carry no explicit version counter. `basketId` + `lastModified` change together on
69	 * every write SFCC accepts (both real fields on the generated `Basket` type), so the pair is a
70	 * workable proxy for "the exact basket state a correction was last attempted against" — this is
71	 * this file's own reasoned choice, not sourced from an existing codebase precedent or doc.
72	 */
73	const getBasketVersionKey = (basket: CartCapBasket): string => `${basket.basketId ?? ''}:${basket.lastModified ?? ''}`;
74	
75	/**
76	 * Storage key for "which basket version has a correction already been attempted against."
77	 * Deliberately not a `useRef` — the post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`) and the
78	 * future render guard (step 4.6) each get their own separate `useCartMergeAndCap()` call, and
79	 * therefore their own separate refs, since they mount in two different React component trees. A
80	 * plain ref cannot coordinate between them. Piggybacking on the already-global `QueryClient` (the
81	 * same one `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard reads from — see that function's
82	 * own comment) via `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` gives real cross-instance-shared storage without
83	 * inventing a new module-level singleton or Context provider. It is also, unlike a React-render-
84	 * time hook value, live/imperative — reading and then
85	 * immediately writing it inside `capBasketQuantities` with no `await` in between (see that
86	 * function) leaves no window for two near-simultaneous calls to both pass the check before either
87	 * has recorded its attempt, since JavaScript runs that synchronous read-then-write as one
88	 * uninterruptible step.
89	 */
90	const CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedBasketVersion'] as const;
91	
92	/**
93	 * Storage key for "which customerId has already claimed the post-sign-in merge." Same
94	 * cross-instance-shared-QueryClient technique as `CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY` above, same reasoning:
95	 * `use-auth-modal.tsx` and `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` each mount their own `useCartMergeAndCap()`
96	 * call, in two different component trees, and each independently reacts to the same
97	 * `isRegistered` transition. Without this, both call `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` for the same
98	 * sign-in event — confirmed live (SFCC-250 round 2 investigation): whichever request the server
99	 * processes second always 409s (the guest basket the first request already consumed is gone),
100	 * and because that second, wasted request is still a real in-flight mutation, it can trip
101	 * `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard above and cause a *correct* correction
102	 * attempt from the winning caller to be silently skipped too — confirmed as the actual mechanism
103	 * behind a merge that summed correctly but was never capped.
104	 *
105	 * Keyed on the customerId being signed into, not a per-instance ref, for the same reason
106	 * `CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY` isn't a ref: two separate component trees need to see the same claim. A
107	 * fresh anonymous customerId is issued for every genuinely new guest session (confirmed live,
108	 * repeatedly, against the real dev SLAS token endpoint), so this key is naturally fresh for every
109	 * real sign-in — no explicit clearing needed. Known, accepted limitation: signing out and back
110	 * into the *same* account a second time, within the same browser tab, without a full page
111	 * reload, would see the second sign-in's merge silently skipped (the first sign-in's claim for
112	 * that customerId is still recorded, and nothing clears it). Not a concern for the bug this
113	 * exists to fix — every real sign-in starts from a distinct guest session — but a genuine
114	 * limitation nonetheless, disclosed here rather than silently accepted.
115	 */
116	const MERGE_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedMergeForCustomerId'] as const;
117	
118	export type UseCartMergeAndCapReturn = {
119	  /**
120	   * Checks every basket line against `getMaxOrderQuantity` and, if any line exceeds its cap,
121	   * issues one `updateItemsInBasket` write reducing every over-cap line to its own max in a
122	   * single request (matching the SFCC-11 plan's "one write" framing even when more than one line
123	   * needs correcting). Resolves only once that write — if one was issued — has fully settled, so
124	   * a caller sequencing merge -> cap -> a future wishlist-resume can `await` this in turn without
125	   * racing it.
126	   */
127	  capBasketQuantities: (basket: CartCapBasket) => Promise<CartCapResult>;
128	  /**
129	   * Resolves once no mutation is in flight anywhere in the app, or `false` if that never happens
130	   * within the bound below.
131	   *
132	   * For a caller that wants to fire its own *non-basket* mutation right after sign-in without
133	   * derailing the merge-then-cap chain. `capBasketQuantities` refuses to run while any mutation
134	   * is in flight (see its own guard) — and that guard is unscoped by necessity, since
135	   * commerce-sdk-react's mutation hooks set no `mutationKey`. So an unrelated write landing in
136	   * the post-merge window makes the cap skip, and the over-cap line survives until something
137	   * later happens to re-trigger a cap attempt at a quiet moment.
138	   *
139	   * Confirmed live (SFCC-11): a guest who adds to wishlist then signs in has
140	   * `createCustomerProductListItem` in flight across exactly that window — merge request at
141	   * 30980ms, wishlist-add request at 31279ms, and every cap attempt from 31251ms onward reporting
142	   * `isMutating: 1` and skipping. The login-only path has no such second mutation, which is why
143	   * it caps correctly and the wishlist path does not.
144	   *
145	   * Deliberately additive: it changes nothing for existing callers, so the already-working
146	   * login-only merge path is untouched.
147	   */
148	  waitForCartWritesToSettle: () => Promise<boolean>;
149	  /**
150	   * Synchronous check-then-claim, called *before* invoking `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` — not after
151	   * — since the whole point is deciding whether to call it at all. Returns `true` exactly once
152	   * per customerId (whichever of the (at most two, today) mounted merge-triggering effects reaches
153	   * it first); every other call for the same customerId returns `false` until a different
154	   * customerId claims it. See `MERGE_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY`'s own comment for why it's keyed this way
155	   * and what it does not cover.
156	   */
157	  claimBasketMerge: (customerId: string) => boolean;
158	};
159	
160	/**
161	 * Hook — the shared "merge coordination + cap" half of SFCC-250's merge-then-cap flow.
162	 * `capBasketQuantities` has two real callers: the post-auth effect inside
163	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `isRegistered` effect, and the cart drawer's always-mounted
164	 * render guard (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`'s own `useEffect(..., [basket])`).
165	 * `claimBasketMerge` has two real callers too, added in the SFCC-250 round-2 fix:
166	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own merge effect and `use-auth-modal.tsx`'s `handleMergeBasket` —
167	 * both independently react to the same `isRegistered` transition, and without a shared claim both
168	 * called `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` for the same sign-in (confirmed live: the loser always 409s,
169	 * and — because it's still a real in-flight mutation — can trip `capBasketQuantities`'s own
170	 * mutation-in-flight guard and cause the *winning* caller's correct cap attempt to be skipped
171	 * too). See `MERGE_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY`'s own comment for the fix and its one disclosed limitation.
172	 *
173	 * Per rules-of-hooks, call this at the top level of whichever hook or component needs it — never
174	 * from inside a `useEffect` callback — and invoke the returned functions themselves from inside
175	 * the effect/render path instead.
176	 *
177	 * @returns `capBasketQuantities` and `claimBasketMerge` — see each's own JSDoc above.
178	 */
179	export const useCartMergeAndCap = (): UseCartMergeAndCapReturn => {
180	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
181	  const updateItemsInBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateItemsInBasket');
182	
183	  const waitForCartWritesToSettle = async (): Promise<boolean> => {
184	    const start = Date.now();
185	    while (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
186	      if (Date.now() - start >= CART_WRITE_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS) {
187	        return false;
188	      }
189	      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, CART_WRITE_SETTLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS));
190	    }
191	    return true;
192	  };
193	
194	  const claimBasketMerge = (customerId: string): boolean => {
195	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(MERGE_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === customerId) {
196	      return false;
197	    }
198	    // Synchronous read-then-write, no `await` between — same reasoning as capBasketQuantities'
199	    // own loop guard below: this is what makes two near-simultaneous callers unable to both read
200	    // "not yet claimed" before either has recorded its own claim.
201	    queryClient.setQueryData(MERGE_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, customerId);
202	    return true;
203	  };
204	
205	  const capBasketQuantities = async (basket: CartCapBasket): Promise<CartCapResult> => {
206	    // No-op while any mutation is in flight (this hook's own prior correction, the merge that
207	    // just ran, a shopper's manual quantity edit — anything) so this can never race a write
208	    // already under way. See this function's own JSDoc.
209	    //
210	    // REWORK (round 1, Tester-confirmed defect): this must be a LIVE read taken at the moment
211	    // this function actually runs — not a React-render-time value closed over at this hook's own
212	    // top level. `capBasketQuantities` is captured once by its caller and invoked later, from
213	    // inside an async callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s `mergeBasket.mutate(...).onSuccess`,
214	    // itself only reachable after a real network round trip) with no guarantee that hook instance
215	    // re-renders in between. A `useIsMutating()` value read at this hook's own top level (the
216	    // original approach here) would still reflect whatever mutation count existed at that earlier
217	    // render, not the real state at the moment this guard actually needs to check it.
218	    //
219	    // `queryClient.isMutating(filters?)` (confirmed against the installed
220	    // `@tanstack/query-core@4.43.0` source — a single deduped version across this project's whole
221	    // dependency tree, per `npm ls @tanstack/react-query` — `node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/
222	    // build/lib/queryClient.esm.js`: `isMutating(filters) { return this.mutationCache.findAll(
223	    // {...filters, fetching: true}).length; }`) computes this fresh from the live mutation cache
224	    // on every call. It is the exact same computation `useIsMutating()` itself wraps in
225	    // `useSyncExternalStore` for React reactivity (`node_modules/@tanstack/react-query/build/lib/
226	    // useIsMutating.esm.js`: `() => queryClient.isMutating(filters)`), just read directly instead
227	    // of through a render-synced subscription — so this preserves the exact same "every mutation
228	    // anywhere in the app" scope this guard has always had (commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation
229	    // hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of
230	    // them), it now just reads that scope live instead of stale.
231	    if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
232	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
233	    }
234	
235	    const correctedItems = (basket.productItems ?? []).filter(needsQuantityCorrection).map((item) => ({
236	      itemId: item.itemId,
237	      productId: item.productId,
238	      quantity: getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item),
239	    }));
240	
241	    if (correctedItems.length === 0) {
242	      return { status: 'not-needed' };
243	    }
244	
245	    if (!basket.basketId) {
246	      // No basketId means there is nothing valid to address a write at — surface this as an
247	      // error rather than silently doing nothing, so a caller can tell "nothing needed fixing"
248	      // apart from "something needed fixing and couldn't be".
249	      return { status: 'error', error: new Error('useCartMergeAndCap: basket is missing a basketId.') };
250	    }
251	
252	    const versionKey = getBasketVersionKey(basket);
253	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === versionKey) {
254	      // Loop guard: a correction has already been attempted against this exact basket state,
255	      // whether it succeeded or failed — do not retry it. See CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY's own
256	      // comment for why this is a live cache read rather than a per-instance ref, and why
257	      // setting it below, before the `await`, is what keeps this race-free.
258	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'already-attempted-this-version' };
259	    }
260	    queryClient.setQueryData(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, versionKey);
261	
262	    try {
263	      await updateItemsInBasket.mutateAsync({
264	        parameters: { basketId: basket.basketId },
265	        body: correctedItems,
266	      });
267	      return { status: 'corrected' };
268	    } catch (error) {
269	      // Surfaced to the caller, not retried: the version is already marked attempted above, so a
270	      // later call against this same unchanged basket state returns 'skipped' rather than
271	      // hammering the server again — no retry storm.
272	      return { status: 'error', error };
273	    }
274	  };
